newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt reimposes ban on some European beef.
newsitem.headline: Egypt reimposes ban on some European beef.

text.p: Egypt has banned imports of live cattle from Ireland, Switzerland, France and Portugal because of mad cow disease, diplomatic sources said on Wednesday.
The ban covers imports of all beef from Switzerland, the country with the highest incidence of the disease after Britain.

A decree from Agriculture Minister Youssef Wali, signed on Monday, also imposes stricter controls on all beef products from countries which have recorded cases of the disease, known as bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE), they said.
The measures are for an initial period of six months, at the end of which the ministry will review them, they said.
The country hardest hit is Ireland, which has at least three shiploads of live cattle already on their way to Egypt, an Irish embassy spokesman said.
In March Irish cows spent days off the Mediterranean port of Alexandria as the Irish government pleaded with the Egyptian authorities to let them land. Egypt eventually relented.
Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak had banned all imports of European beef, soon after scientists announced there could be a link between BSE and its human equivalent.
Egypt later lifted the ban on imports from European countries other than Britain, which has the highest BSE rate.
The diplomats said the new ban was based on the changing incidence of BSE in the four countries affected. Ireland, for example, had 73 cases in 1996, compared with 19 in 1995. JW ME
